# 0087. A project map is generated by hostd from its mirror and kept under the work root

- **Status:** accepted
- **Date:** 2026-11-26

## Context

The crew starts every task with no memory of the repository. Each time, it
works out again where the packages are, what each one owns, where its entry
point and tests are, which ADRs matter and which paths need a person's review.
#379 gives every managed repository a generated summary of that, the project
map, which the crew keeps current. #380 shows it and puts it in a session's
context.

Several constraints shaped the decision:

- The map must not change the repository.
- It must carry no credential.
- It must carry no text from people without access to the repository, and no
  `openadlc:` marker that a session could mistake for its own.
- It must follow the default branch without anyone asking.
- The GitHub app is not subscribed to `push`. Subscribing would change the
  app's manifest and events under `config/`, a Human-review path.

## Decision

- **Where it lives.** The map is a file under hostd's work root,
  `<workRoot>/maps/<owner>__<name>.md`: folder 0700, file 0600, one per
  managed repository. It is never committed, and there is no table. Its
  header holds the commit it was built from and when it was built. A failed
  attempt's reason is kept in hostd's memory until its next attempt, and the
  `project-map` health card reads it through `GET /project-maps`.
- **How it is built.** It is generated by plain code
  (`apps/hostd/src/project-map.ts`), not a model. The code reads the default
  branch's tree in the tasks' own mirror, fetched under `withMirrorLock`
  with the automation bot's token in git's environment only. It reads with
  `git ls-tree` and `git cat-file` and checks nothing out, so nothing of the
  repository runs. No branch but the default one is read, so the map carries
  only merged text, which only people with access can merge.
- **How it is refreshed.** By polling, plus a nudge after each merge. The
  bridge's `maps` job (`OPENADLC_JOB_MAPS_MINUTES`, every 15 minutes) asks
  hostd for each repository in turn. hostd rebuilds only when the default
  branch's commit moved. The merge job asks for a pass after it merged
  something, without waiting for it. The first pass after the bridge starts,
  and one every 24 hours after that, is forced, which is the nightly rebuild.
- **What makes it deterministic.** Every line is a function of the tree at the
  commit, except `Built at`. Paths sort by code unit, never by locale, and
  nothing from the environment or the remote URL goes in. The file is written
  only when the commit, the format version or the body changed, so `Built at`
  changes only with them, and the same commit gives the same bytes. A write is
  a tmp file, `fsync`, then `rename`, so a failure keeps the previous map whole.
- **How text is sanitised.** Every string taken from a file goes through
  `redactSecrets` and loses HTML comments, `<!--` and `-->`. It is folded to
  one line and capped at 400 characters, cut at a sentence's end where there
  is one. Blobs over 256 KiB are not read.

## What this rules out

- **A `push` webhook.** It would change the app's manifest and its events under
  `config/`, a Human-review path, and it would still miss a delivery that never
  arrived. A quarter-hourly look at the mirror's head catches every move,
  including a person's merge on GitHub.
- **A mirror of its own for the map, as release builds have.** That is a
  second copy of every repository with no isolation gained, since nothing here
  runs the repository's code. Sharing the tasks' mirror also keeps it warm for
  the next task.
- **Generating the map in a task session, with a model.** That would cost money
  on every refresh, and its output would not be deterministic.
- **Committing the map, or keeping it in a table.** Committing would write into
  the repository on every merge. A table would add a migration for what one
  file's header already holds. Letting a repository opt in to committing its
  map was left for a follow-up.
- **Reading a worktree or any branch but the default.** That could carry
  unmerged text, including text from people without access, into a session's
  context.

## What would make this worth revisiting

- The app subscribes to `push` for another reason. A push could then trigger
  the refresh directly, and the poll could become a backstop only.
- The map has to be read by something other than the bridge on the same host,
  such as a second hostd or a remote console. A file under one host's work root
  would no longer be the right store.
- People start wanting text in the map that plain code cannot extract
  deterministically.
